identity.title: Consistency Checks for Language Model Forecasters

problem.claim: Forecasting systems need evaluation before future ground truth is available.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a need for instantaneous benchmarking of LLM forecasters, whose eventual ground-truth performance cannot yet be observed.

contributions.claim: A general arbitrage-based consistency metric for logically related forecasts.
An automated pipeline that generates base questions, instantiates consistency checks, elicits predictions, and measures consistency.
A standard proper-scoring-rule benchmark and a consistency benchmark resolving in 2028.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose a new general consistency metric based on arbitrage.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that instantaneous consistency metrics correlate strongly with LLM forecasters' eventual ground-truth Brier scores.
The authors report releasing a consistency benchmark designed for long-term evaluation through 2028.

narrative_sequence.summary: Forecasting is difficult to evaluate immediately because ground truth arrives only in the future.
The paper evaluates forecasters through consistency across logically related questions and proposes an arbitrage-based metric.
An automated system generates questions and checks, collects forecasts, and scores their consistency.
The authors compare consistency with eventual Brier scores and release a benchmark resolving in 2028.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns an instantaneous proxy metric with a delayed proper-scoring-rule outcome.

lessons.interpretation: A proxy is more interpretable when its relationship to a recognized eventual measure is stated explicitly.
lessons.application: When proposing an early evaluation signal, define the delayed target and report the proxy–target relationship in the same study.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when no credible delayed target exists or when the proxy and target measure materially different tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the strength or statistical details of the reported correlation.
It does not describe the question-generation procedure, benchmark composition, or how arbitrage profit is calculated.
The 2028 benchmark's current size and evaluation protocol are unspecified.
